title: Farther the Shift, Sparser the Representation: Analyzing OOD Mechanisms in LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2603.03415v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: In this work, we investigate how the internal representations of Large Language Models (LLMs) change with inputs of increasing difficulty. Although sparsity changes may not be obvious for individual samples, dataset-level results reveal a consistent statistical trend: as task difficulty increases (e.g., harder questions, longer contexts, or more answer choices), the last hidden states of LLMs become systematically sparser. In short, \textbf{the harder the task, the sparser the representation}. This sparsity--difficulty relation is observable across diverse models and domains, suggesting that harder inputs drive more concentrated activation patterns in the last hidden state. translated_title: 偏移越远，表征越稀疏：分析大语言模型中的分布外（OOD）机制
translated_abstract: 在本工作中，我们研究了随着输入难度的增加，大语言模型（LLM）的内部表征如何发生变化。尽管在单个样本层面稀疏度的变化可能并不明显，但在数据集层面的结果揭示了一个一致的统计趋势：随着任务难度的提升（例如更难的问题、更长的上下文或更多的答案选项），LLM最后一层隐藏状态会系统性地变得更加稀疏。简而言之，任务越难，表征越稀疏。这种稀疏度与难度的关系在多种模型和领域中均可观察到，表明更难的输入会促使最后一层隐藏状态中的激活模式更加集中。通过一系列受控分析和学习动态实验，我们证明表征密度是模型对数据熟悉度的一种习得属性：模型会为已掌握的模式发展出丰富且分布式的表征，而面对陌生的输入时则表现出……
tldr: 本文揭示了LLM内部表征的稀疏度随任务难度增加而系统性增大——任务越难，最后一层隐藏状态的表征越稀疏，且该规律跨模型、跨领域普遍成立，表明表征密度是模型对数据熟悉度的习得属性。
en_tdlr: This work reveals that LLM internal representations become systematically sparser as task difficulty increases—harder tasks yield sparser last-hidden-state representations across models and domains, showing that representational density is a learned property of data familiarity.
